summary: Seán McLoughlin works in religious studies and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Manchester and served as a Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds, attested in 2005.

Shailendra Bhandare is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has held positions at the British Museum and Fitzwilliam Museum, served as Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022), and became a Fellow of St Cross College, Oxford (attested 2022).
Shan Shan Zhao is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University, where she was supervised by James A. Benn and also studied under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shane McCausland (born 1968) specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Princeton University from 1996 to 2000 and held a post at SOAS University of London in 2009.
Shanshan Jia is a scholar of Indology. Attested in 2015, she pursued doctoral studies in Indology at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Harunaga Isaacson.

Shaoyong Ye specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Peking University by 2009 under the supervision of Qing Duan (attested 2007–2008), and served there as Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016).

Sharon J. Roe specializes in religious studies and philosophy. Attested in 2014, she pursued her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the doctoral supervision of Steven D. Goodman.
Sharon Salzberg (born 1952) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University at Buffalo from circa 1969 to 1973 and received traditional training under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta (1911–1964) was an Indian scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, where he held a Premchand Roychand Studentship (~1937) and served as Lecturer (~1945–1964).

Shayne Clarke is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury (MA, 1998–1999), and UCLA (PhD, -2006). Attested in 2015–2016, he served as Associate Professor at McMaster University.
Shek-wing Tam (1935–2024) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche (~1972–1987) and held a post at Renmin University of China.

Sheldon Pollock (born 1948) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Harvard University (~1971–1975). He held posts at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago (1989–2005), and Columbia University (2005–2022), alongside the Clay Sanskrit Library.

Sheng Yen (1931–2009) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a doctorate at Rissho University (~1969–1975). He held posts at National Cheng Kung University and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1985–2009), founding Dharma Drum Mountain.

Shenghai Li specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, supervised by Donald R. Davis Jr. and Charles Hallisey (attested 2012), and studied under traditional teachers and other scholars including Gudrun Bühnemann.

Shenpen Hookham (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under several traditional teachers, including Kalu Rinpoche, and earned a D.Phil from the University of Oxford (~1981–1986) under doctoral supervisor Michael M. Broido.

Shi Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007). He held a post at the University of Hong Kong and later served as a professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2013).

Shichang Ma (1934–2018) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He served as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.
Shigeki Kudo (born 1931) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has held academic appointments at Kyoto University, Shuchiin University, and Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. A specialist in Buddhist studies and sinology, he served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1988), Aichi Gakuin University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Otani University (~1958–1963), Ryukoku University (1962), and Koyasan University (~1974–1988).
